standard_prerequisites.name: Support of a finite module over a Noetherian local ring and finiteness of the length at a minimal prime of the support
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-support-point (Stacks tag 00L5), invoked at proof line 17982
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that q is a minimal prime of the support exactly when M_q has finite length, which is what makes l = length_{R_q}(M_q) finite and the sequence y_1, ..., y_l available; the lifting and clearing of denominators is inside the counted span.

core_obligations: Use that q a minimal prime of the support of M makes l = length_{R_q}(M_q) finite, and choose y_1, ..., y_l in M_q with successive quotients kappa(q) (proof lines 17980-17986).

Lift each y_i to M after multiplying by a scalar f_i not in q, and use Noetherianity to write q = (g_1, ..., g_t) so that each g_j annihilates y_i modulo <y_1, ..., y_{i-1}> in M_q (proof lines 17987-17996).

Clear the finitely many arising denominators f_{ij} not in q to obtain equalities f_{ij} g_j z_i in <z_1, ..., z_{i-1}> inside the module M itself, and set x_i to be the product of all f's up to and including the i-th block times z_i (proof lines 17993-18003).

Conclude the two required properties: the localisations R_q x_1 + ... + R_q x_i modulo R_q x_1 + ... + R_q x_{i-1} are one dimensional over kappa(q), and q x_i lies in <x_1, ..., x_{i-1}>, so <x_1, ..., x_i>/<x_1, ..., x_{i-1}> is a one-generator R-module annihilated by q that becomes one dimensional after localising at q, hence is isomorphic to R/q; and the support of M/<x_1, ..., x_l> at q is empty because the localisations generate M_q (proof lines 18003-18013).
proof_roadmap: Get the finite sequence in the localisation from the finiteness of the length at the minimal prime (proof lines 17980-17986).
Lift with f_i not in q and record the annihilation by the generators g_j of q (proof lines 17987-17996).
Clear the denominators f_{ij} to work inside M, and verify the two properties of the resulting x_i (proof lines 17997-18013).
difficulty_reason: For a finite module M over a local Noetherian ring R and a prime q that is a minimal prime of the support of M, the lemma produces elements x_1, ..., x_l of M such that the support of M/<x_1, ..., x_l> misses q while each successive quotient <x_1, ..., x_i>/<x_1, ..., x_{i-1}> is isomorphic to R/q, and it adds that necessarily l = length_{R_q}(M_q) (statement lines 17963-17977). The proof is a clearing-of-denominators argument rather than a citation: it takes a chain y_1, ..., y_l in the localisation M_q with the required successive quotients, lifts f_i y_i to elements z_i of M with f_i not in q, writes q = (g_1, ..., g_t) by Noetherianity, records that g_j y_i lies in <y_1, ..., y_{i-1}> after localising, and clears the finitely many denominators f_{ij} not in q to get f_{ij} g_j z_i in <z_1, ..., z_{i-1}> inside M; the products of the f's times z_i then have the required property because all cleared scalars are invertible at q, and each quotient is a one-generator R-module annihilated by q whose localisation at q is one dimensional over kappa(q), hence is R/q (proof lines 17980-18013). That last identification and the length statement are the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.
